title: Maximum Score Using Exactly K Pairs
summary: Given integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of lengths n and m, and an integer k, select exactly k pairs (i, j) such that 0 <= i < j < n and 0 <= j < k < m to maximize the total score.
statement: Given integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of lengths n and m, and an integer k, select exactly k pairs (i, j) such that 0 <= i < j < n and 0 <= j < k < m to maximize the total score. The score for each pair (i, j) is nums1[i] * nums2[j], and the total score is the sum of these products.
constraints: Both arrays are nonempty, contain signed integers, and k does not exceed either length.
Choose increasing indices i1<…<ik and j1<…<jk.
Maximize the sum of nums1[it]×nums2[jt] over the k position-preserving pairs.
hints: The final choice either skips an element or pairs the current elements after an optimal smaller-prefix solution.
Track the best score by second-array prefix and number of completed pairs while sweeping the first array.
Copy skip states, propagate skips in nums2, and extend only the previous first-array row at j-1.
Those three transitions cover every ordered matching, while using the previous row prevents reusing a nums1 element.
